en.title: Selecting the Maximum from a Queue in Rounds
en.description: Given n non-negative integers and an integer x, perform x rounds. In each round, take up to x numbers from the front of the queue and select the maximum among them; on ties, select the one closest to the front. Decrease each of the other values by 1 (to a minimum of 0) and put them back at the end of the queue in their original relative order. Output the original 1-based indices of the selected elements.
en.input: The first line contains n and x, and the second line contains n non-negative integers. Site limits: 1≤x≤n≤1000, 0≤queue[i]≤10⁹. x≤n is a site limit that guarantees the queue is non-empty at the start of every round.
en.output: Output the original indices of the x selected elements in the order they were selected, separated by spaces.
en.explanation: The original sample input came without an output. Simulating round by round according to the original text, the indices selected for that sample are 5 6 7 4 1; this result was recomputed by this site and is not presented as the source's answer.
hints: In each round, first take out the first x items of the current queue and record the first maximum, then decrement the remaining elements and put them back in order.
